title: Add Two Numbers
statement_short: Given two non-empty linked lists representing two non-negative integers stored in reverse order, add the two numbers and return the sum as a linked list. Each node contains a single digit.
constraints: 1 <= number of nodes <= 100, 0 <= Node.val <= 9, it is guaranteed that the list represents a number that does not have leading zeros
hint: List length up to 100 allows a simple single-pass node addition with carry propagation.
why_not: Right: Math / Geometry applies schoolbook column addition, managing digit sums and carry values in O(max(m, n)) time. Not Stack: Reversing digit order with a stack is unnecessary since input digits are already stored in reverse order (least significant digit first). Not HashMap / Hash Set: Storing node values in hash tables adds unnecessary memory overhead for linear traversal. Not 1D DP: Storing state subproblems is unneeded for single-pass digit addition with carry propagation.
complexity: O(max(m, n)) time, O(max(m, n)) space
